name: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
aliases: Primary cutaneous large B-cell lymphoma, leg type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Diffuse dermal infiltrate of large atypical B-cells with centroblastic or immunoblastic morphology
Expression of B-cell markers CD20+, MUM1/IRF4+, BCL2+, and frequent absence of CD10 and BCL6
Solitary or multiple rapidly growing nodules or tumors localized predominantly on the legs
No evidence of extracutaneous lymphoma at diagnosis
Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement supporting B-cell clonality

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation on the leg, histopathological confirmation of diffuse large B-cell infiltrate with characteristic immunophenotype, and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging erythematous to violaceous nodules or tumors on the lower legs
searchTerms: rapidly enlarging skin lumps on legs
quickly growing tumors on lower legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse dermal infiltration by large atypical B-cells confirmed histologically
searchTerms: dense immune cell presence in skin

common.symptomName: B-symptoms including low-grade fever and night sweats
Tenderness or pain at lesion sites

occasional.notes: May be present but not always involved

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated lesions

rare.symptomName: Dissemination to extracutaneous sites such as bone marrow or central nervous system
rare.notes: Rare at initial diagnosis but possible in advanced disease
searchTerms: spread to bone marrow or brain
immune system attacks related to cancer

laboratory: Elevated LDH levels in some cases
Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, MUM1, BCL2
imaging: MRI or ultrasound of affected leg lesions
other: Histopathology showing diffuse large B-cell infiltrate
Exclusion of systemic lymphoma by bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Usually presents with localized plaques or nodules on head or trunk
Small B-cell infiltrate with plasmacytic differentiation
Often presents as papules or plaques
Generally negative for BCL2 and MUM1
Systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy present at diagnosis

redFlags: Rapid progression of cutaneous tumors on the legs
Ulceration and secondary infection of skin lesions
Evidence of systemic dissemination or extracutaneous involvement
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Pileri SA, et al. The 2016 revision of the World Health Organization classification of lymphoid neoplasms. Blood. 2016.
Grange F, Beylot-Barry M, Petrella T, et al. Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type: a review of clinical, histopathological and molecular features. Br J Dermatol. 2012.
Orphanet: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type. ORPHA:178544.
